resources.string: Not connected to a hub yet
Ask whoever looks after your hub for an invitation, and scan its code with this phone.
This phone cannot scan codes right now. Paste the invitation link instead.
That is not an invitation to a hub. Ask for the code or the link again.
Paste the link from your invitation.
That is not an address. It looks like hub.local:5002.
A hub\'s address starts with http:// or https://.
Only the hub\'s address, with nothing after it.
Plain http:// is only for addresses on your home network. Use https:// for this one.
The hub did not answer. Check the address, and that this phone is on the same network as the hub.
The hub did not answer in time. Try again in a moment.
This address leads outside your home network, where plain http:// is not safe. Use https:// for it.
Something answered that is not a hub. Check the address, and whether this Wi-Fi wants you to sign in first.
The hub is refusing further attempts for now. Wait a few minutes.
The hub failed while handling that. Try again later.
Something went wrong while talking to the hub. Try again.
Your hub is on the network this phone is connected to. Android asks before an app reaches devices there, so it will ask you next.
Without access to devices on your network, this app cannot reach your hub. Allow it in this app\'s permissions in the settings.
This invitation connects this phone to the hub at %1$s. It works once.
This invitation is more than 15 minutes old, so it has run out. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
This invitation does not work any more. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
No usable answer came back, so the invitation may already have been used. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
The hub did not accept that username and password.
It ends within a day. Opening the app on your home network renews it.

resources.string: The hub no longer accepts this phone. The session may have run out, or the account may have been disabled or removed. Ask for a new invitation to connect again.
